Name: Dr. Astha Arora
Research Area: Decision-Making, Cognitive-Emotional Processing & Social Cognitive Neuroscience
Description: Investigated neuroelectrical responses underlying decisions to escalate or de-escalate commitment across personal-professional and professional relationship contexts, examining the role of cognitive-emotional interplay.
Tools: 64-Channel EEG, ERP, P300, N200/N260, Behavioural Decision Tasks
Results: Demonstrated differences in frontal and parietal ERP responses across decision contexts, highlighting neural differences associated with escalation and de-escalation decisions.

Name: Dr. Mona Arthi Efcibha M. S.
Description: Examined neuroelectrical responses to nostalgic advertising to understand the cognitive and emotional processes involved in consumer responses to nostalgia-based marketing stimuli.
Results: Examined neural responses associated with nostalgic advertising and their relevance to consumer cognition and emotional processing.

Name: Dr. Sayujya
Description: Used physiological parameters such as respiration, pulse rate, and oxygen saturation levels under olfactory stimulation during visual psychomotor activity.
Tools: Respiratory belt, pulse oximeter, driving simulator, and psychometric tools
Results: Olfactory stimulation based on peppermint and rosemary has a positive effect on psychophysiological parameters.
